stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}(x - 1)^{n}}{n\,5^{n}} \) for \( |x - 1| < 5 \). A partial sum made of the first \( N \) terms of this series at \( x = 3 \) is used to approximate \( f\left(3\right) \). Find the least \( N \) for which the alternating series error bound guarantees that the error is at most \( \frac{1}{100} \).

worked_solution.text: At \( x = 3 \), \( x - 1 = 2 \), so the series alternates with terms \( a_n = \frac{(\frac{2}{5})^{n}}{n} \) that decrease to 0.
With \( N \) terms, the error is at most the first omitted term \( a_{N+1} \).
Here \( a_{3} = \frac{8}{375} \) is larger than \( \frac{1}{100} \) but \( a_{4} = \frac{4}{625} \) is at most \( \frac{1}{100} \).
So \( N = 3 \) terms are enough, and no smaller \( N \) is guaranteed by the bound.
